title.narrative: 2024/25 Provision of Winter Heating Fuel for Frontline Households in Zaporizhzhia and Kharkivska Oblasts

description.narrative: ltpgtWith more than 60% of Ukraine’s energy infrastructure damaged or destroyed since 2022 and the war in a relative stalemate, heating needs for the 2024-25 winter season are anticipated to again be substantial, especially in Eastern and Southern Oblasts (“the crescent”) which have sustained the highest levels of damage (World Bank). ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtIn alignment with needs assessments, community consultations on modality preference, market monitoring and sectoral guidance, CORE proposes to deliver life-saving winter assistance from August 2024 - March 2025 via the in-kind distribution of heating fuel to vulnerable households in four hromadas near the frontline (10-70km) in Kharkivska (Balakliyska, Oskilvska) and Zaporizhzhia (Orikhivska, Novolekandrivska) Oblasts. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtIn the East, households face multiple barriers – including resource availability, market access, lack of transport, winter conditions, and security conditions – to securing sufficient heating resources to maintain adequate body temperatures in winter. It is probable the on-going Russian attacks on energy and utility infrastructure will continue even as temperatures drop, requiring household-based heating solutions to avoid negative health outcomes for vulnerable, frontline households, including illness, hypothermia, and death. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe surge in demand for alternative solid heating fuels, such as firewood and briquettes, during wartime has driven supply shortages and price increases in the previous two winters. With savings and coping strategies depleted after over two years of war and scarce livelihoods opportunities, households on the frontline report they will be hard pressed to afford these life-saving resources for winter. Moreover, markets in the targeted hromadas are not adequately functioning to enable cash assistance as a preferred modality of support, and landmines and ongoing insecurity create challenges for households to secure and transport sufficient heating fuel for winter (REACH JMMI 5/2023). Supply chain disruptions have also diminished the level of resources available on the market and many vulnerable households (older persons, people with disabilities (PwD)) experience additional mobility barriers to reach markets (CARE). To overcome these challenges, CORE and partners, 100% Life Zaporizhzhia (100% Life) and Southern Development Strategy (SDS), will distribute in-kind heating fuel to 2,850 of the most vulnerable households in Zaporizhzhia (1200HH) and Kharkivska (1650HH) Oblasts. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtCORE, 100% Life, and SDS anticipate providing 2 rounds of home delivery of heating fuel during the winter (Oct/Nov and January) to avoid supply availability constraints and household storage issues. Based on information on preferences for heating fuel types in CORE’s July 2024 Winter Needs Assessment, households will receive firewood to cover their winter energy needs in all hromadas. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtCORE will manage project administration, fuel procurement and logistics, operation of the feedback and accountability mechanism (FAM), monitoring and evaluation functions, and reporting. 100% Life and SDS will liaise with local officials, engage in beneficiary identification, manage transportation and handling, and conduct distribution/delivery to households. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtCORE and partners will follow vulnerability-based guidance on targeting from the Shelter/NFI 2024-25 Ukraine Winterization Recommendations to prioritize household selection. Beyond prioritizing households in frontline areas not receiving other government assistance, CORE will prioritize inclusion of women-headed households, older persons, PwD, families with 3+ children, pregnant and lactating women, and persons with chronic illness or conditions.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtCORE will engage its robust procurement capacity and conduct bulk orders to secure the required amount of heating fuel at competitive prices. In-kind heating fuel will be ordered ahead of the season and delivered in two tranches to avoid contributing to supply chain constraints and household storage issues.lt/pgt
